question: Does a Canadian record suspension erase the conviction from my record entirely?
generated_answer:
No. You must still answer "yes" on an employment application if you are asked if you have ever been convicted of a criminal offence. However, a record suspension does not prevent you from receiving a Canadian passport, or prohibit you from travelling outside Canada. How do I know if I am eligible for a record suspension? To be eligible for a record suspension under the Criminal Records Act, a specified period of time must have elapsed after the end of the sentence imposed. This is the period of good conduct. To be eligible for a record suspension, you must have been convicted under a federal Act or regulation and have been convicted in Canada, or been convicted under a federal Act or regulation and have been sentenced in Canada. You may also apply if you were convicted under an Act of the Parliament of Canada from before 1992 that was later replaced by a federal Act or regulation, and if the offence is no longer an offence under an Act of Parliament. You are not eligible if you have been convicted of a sexual offence involving a child and you are currently designated, or if you are currently serving a court-ordered sentence, including probation, conditional sentence or parole. You are also not eligible if you are convicted of an offence referred to in Schedule 1 of the Criminal Records Act. For a record suspension under the Criminal Records Act, the period during which you cannot apply is as follows:

• if you were convicted of an offence that was prosecuted summarily, you must wait one year after the completion of your sentence; • if you were convicted of an offence that was prosecuted by way of indictment, you must wait three years after the completion of your sentence. What is the application process? All applications must be sent to the Board. For the necessary forms and to obtain a list of the documentation required, you can visit the Board's website at www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/pardon/ or call the Board at 1-800-874-2652. You may wish to seek the assistance of a lawyer, a community legal clinic, or a local John Howard Society to help you fill out the application forms. You must provide complete information about the convictions and sentences you want to have pardoned. You must also provide three character references, which can be signed by people who know you personally, such as family members, neighbours, co-workers and employers. In addition to the above, you must provide the Board with the following documents:

• a certified copy of your criminal record from the Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP) Criminal Records
• a certified copy of your court record from the Clerk of the Court of Appeal or the Clerk of the
• Provincial Court in the province where you were convicted. You must also give the Board a certified copy of your driving record from the provincial or territorial department of transport that issued your driver's licence. If you have been convicted of a sexual offence involving a child, you must give the Board a certified copy of your record of non-payment of child support. Where can I get copies of my criminal record, court record and driving record? To get a certified copy of your criminal record, you must contact the RCMP Criminal Records Records and Identification Services Division at the following address:

• RCMP Criminal Records Records and Identification Services Division CPCS
P.O. Box 8786 Ottawa ON K1G 3M8

For more information, call the RCMP at 1-800-874-2652. To get a certified copy of your court record, you must contact the Clerk of the Court of Appeal or the Clerk of the Provincial Court in the province where you were convicted. For more information about where to get a certified copy of your court record, you can visit the Board's website at www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/pardon/ or call the Board at 1-800-874-2652. To get a certified copy of your driving record, you must contact the provincial or territorial department of transport that issued your driver's licence. For more information about where to get a certified copy of your driving record, you can visit the Board's website at www.rcmp-grc.gc.ca/pardon/ or call the Board at 1-800-874-2652. What will the Board do with my application? The Board will review your application to make sure you are eligible and that all the necessary documentation is included. If your application is incomplete, the Board will contact you and give you time to provide the missing information. The Board may refuse to order a record suspension if the Board is not satisfied that you were of good conduct. The Board will notify you if your application has been refused and give you the reasons for the refusal. The Board will also notify you if your application has been approved. If your application has been approved, the Board will order that your criminal record be suspended and notify the RCMP.
